title: Seeing AI gives a woman with retinitis pigmentosa audio access to printed recipes in a Vanderbilt rehabilitation case report
summary: A 62-year-old with autosomal dominant RP used Microsoft Seeing AI to read printed recipes in her kitchen (case report, 2025).
account: A case report in Case Reports in Ophthalmological Medicine (author at Vanderbilt University Medical Center; published 1 September 2025) describes comprehensive low-vision rehabilitation. The patient was a 62-year-old woman with autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa, best-corrected acuity 20/40–2 and severely constricted visual fields in both eyes. The rehabilitation included optical aids, white cane training and counseling. After the evaluation visit she was referred to Tennessee's blind and independent living skills training program. At the insistence of her independent living skills trainer she met a Technology Access Program specialist. She downloaded free iPhone apps, among them volunteer-based Be My Eyes and Seeing AI. Seeing AI uses the phone camera to turn printed material into auditory output. The report does not name Seeing AI's maker. The Microsoft attribution rests on the app's App Store listing. At a later meeting of the clinic's bimonthly support group, she reported using both applications in the kitchen. Seeing AI helped her access printed recipes. The author declares no conflicts of interest. Visit dates are not given.
purpose: Read printed text aloud for people with visual impairment using computer vision
system: Microsoft Seeing AI smartphone app (computer-vision text recognition to speech)
deployer: Vision rehabilitation clinic (author's department, Vanderbilt University Medical Center), which referred the patient to the state of Tennessee's blind and independent living skills training program; a Technology Access Program specialist introduced the apps; the patient used them at home

ratings.reason: An identifiable patient gained audio access to printed recipes in her kitchen. The report documents this single functional use within a broader rehabilitation plan. The gain is small.
Single case report. The app is widely available but no population effect is shown here.

ai_role.statement: Seeing AI's computer-vision text recognition is what converts the printed recipe into speech. The report lists it alongside non-AI aids (Be My Eyes volunteers, optical devices). It attributes recipe access specifically to Seeing AI.

headline: Seeing AI reads printed recipes aloud for a woman with RP

comparator.against: reading print through her habitual spectacle lenses
comparator.before: She was having trouble reading printed materials, specifically recipes and food preparation instructions, through her habitual spectacle lenses
comparator.after: Seeing AI helping her to access printed recipes
comparator.quote: The patient was using both applications in the kitchen, with Seeing AI helping her to access printed recipes and Be My Eyes allowing her to check expiration dates on food products and set her oven and stove dials accurately.
